vopros: I run a small service business in Los Angeles and customers keep haggling on price. Who in LA can help me with that?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Good news — there are several **free, LA-based resources** specifically set up to help small business owners with pricing, negotiation, and customer strategy. Here's where to go:

## 1. LA Regional SBDC Network (Small Business Development Centers)
This is probably your best bet. The LA Small Business Development Center provides solutions for small business owners through one-on-one advising, innovative workshops, and in-depth programs, at no cost, across Los Angeles, Santa Barbara and Ventura Counties. They literally run a workshop for this exact problem — a course designed to equip participants with the knowledge and skills necessary to effectively price their products or services for maximum profitability and market success.

There are multiple SBDC locations depending on where you're based:
- **Pacific Coast Regional SBDC** (central LA) — their consultants include CEOs, entrepreneurs, MBAs, Ivy League alumni and Fortune 500 execs; reach them at 213.674.2696
- **Pasadena City College SBDC** (San Gabriel Valley)
- **College of the Canyons SBDC** (San Fernando/Santa Clarita Valley) — serving the SFV, SCV & AV, the SBDC provides free one on one consulting services & low cost training
- **Long Beach SBDC** — offers no-cost business advising covering business planning, financials, management, operations, marketing strategizing, and understanding how to sell
- **University of La Verne SBDC** (East San Gabriel Valley)

You can find the one nearest you at smallbizla.org.

## 2. SCORE LA
SCORE LA engages a network of former business owners and executives to provide free business consulting, mentoring and professional guidance to existing and emerging small businesses. They're great for one-on-one mentorship if you want ongoing advice from someone who's run a similar service business before.

## 3. City of LA BusinessSource Centers
BusinessSource Centers provide startup ventures and current small business owners with free and cost-effective tools to make their businesses a success, so small businesses can grow and remain competitive, at no cost to business owners within Los Angeles. They also offer no-cost one-on-one business consultations to aspiring and current business owners.

## 4. LAEDC Business Assistance Program
The Los Angeles County Economic Development Corporation is a nonprofit focused on equitable economic growth, and its Business Assistance Program team offers confidential, free-of-charge consulting to large and small businesses, startup business help, and microenterprises across all industry sectors.

---

### My practical take
For a haggling/pricing issue specifically, I'd start with an **SBDC pricing strategy session** since they have a dedicated workshop for it, and pair it with a **SCORE mentor** who's actually run a service business — they can give you tactical scripts for handling price objections in real conversations, not just theory. All of these are free, so there's no downside to booking a session with two of them and comparing advice.
